audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 4-5, 6 and 2+ items disagree with the packet and the mirror.
audit.why: Packet reads Skill, Irelia, Irelia, Irelia, Irelia, Irelia, Skill against a 45.59% Swain win rate; the page gives Swain-neutral rows exactly where its own mid text says 'Irelia owns this lane'. The mirror already flipped the same rows.
audit.corrected: win[3]/phases[3].side and win[4]/phases[4].side to Irelia; win[6]/phases[6].side to Skill.

audit.why: Spike timings are right — her 2-3 window, her level 6, your level 3 combo, her Trinity Force — but spikes[1] described an ability she does not have.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two invented interactions, each stated more than once: Defiant Dance 'eats/blocks your Q burst', and Vanguard's Edge is 'an AoE knock-up' that chains CC to stop your drain.
audit.why: Riot's text for Defiant Dance says she takes reduced PHYSICAL damage during the charge — Swain deals magic damage, so it blunts nothing you throw. Vanguard's Edge fires blades that damage and Mark, then form a wall that damages and slows what walks through it; there is no knock-up in the text and no knockup flag on the kit. And Demonic Ascension is a transform with no channel, so nothing 'stops' the drain — the wall makes you unable to follow her out of the 650 range, which is the real problem for a Swain with no dash.
audit.corrected: Defiant Dance stated as physical-only; the ultimate described as a Mark plus a blade wall that cuts your retreat and your drain range.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal is only boilerplate in the item line.
audit.why: Bladesurge heals her on every strike and refreshes on a Marked or dying target, so her sustain scales with how many resets the wave offers — Grievous Wounds timing is what decides an extended trade.
Flawless Duet is the right cooldown to track, at 16 seconds rank 1 falling to 10 — long enough that a spent stun really is your window.

edits.before: With passive stacks and Bladesurge resets through the wave Irelia can reach you without walking into W, and her W passive eats your Q burst; she dictates every trade in this window.
edits.after: Bladesurge resets carry her through the wave without entering W range and Ionian Fervor stacks attack speed on top — Defiant Dance cuts physical damage, not your magic, but she still dictates.

edits.before: Her ult adds an AoE knock-up she chains off Flawless Duet, chaining hard CC that stops your Demonic Ascension drain before it heals anything meaningful.
edits.after: Vanguard's Edge leaves a blade wall behind her, and with no dash you cannot cross it — she does not cut your drain, she steps out of its 650 range.

edits.before: Irelia's ult gives her an AoE knock-up she can set up behind Flawless Duet, letting her chain hard CC so your Demonic Ascension can't even sustain the window.
edits.after: Vanguard's Edge Marks you and drops a wall that damages and slows whatever crosses it — with no dash of your own, that wall is what ends your drain, not a CC chain.

edits.before: Use W passive to block your Q burst during the all-in window and sustain through your poke
edits.after: Charge Defiant Dance against physical damage and heal your chip back through Bladesurge resets

edits.before: From level 4 through 6 Irelia owns this lane if she is even or ahead. Her Bladesurge resets on low-health minions mean she can gap-close through the wave to reach you without ever walking into W range, and her W passive blocks the Q burst she knows is coming. Your job is strict cooldown tracking: the only time you commit the full W-slow-into-E pattern is when you confirm Flawless Duet is down and she has no reset path through the wave. If she has stacks on her passive she is trading at a stat advantage on top of the kit advantage — do not extended trade, root and walk away. At level 6 your R sustain is real but she answers with her own ult knock-up chain that locks you in place while her resets do the work; R alone does not flip this lane.
edits.after: From level 4 through 6 Irelia owns this lane if she is even or ahead. Bladesurge resets on dying minions let her reach you through the wave without entering W range, and every strike heals her — carry Grievous Wounds or the chip you land is refunded. Defiant Dance does not blunt your burst, though: it reduces physical damage only, so a charged W is not a reason to hold Q. Track her stun instead: commit the W-slow-into-E pattern only with Flawless Duet confirmed down and no reset path through the wave. With Ionian Fervor stacked she is trading at a stat advantage too — root and leave rather than extend. At 6 her wall, not her CC, is what ends your drain; R alone does not flip this.

notes: Two fabricated interactions, each repeated: Defiant Dance was said to block or eat your Q burst — Riot's text reduces PHYSICAL damage only, and Swain's kit is entirely magic, so that advice made players hold burst for no reason. And Vanguard's Edge was described twice as an AoE knock-up that chains CC to stop Demonic Ascension; it Marks, then leaves a wall that damages and slows. The form has no channel to stop — the wall matters because Swain has no dash and cannot follow her out of the 650 drain radius. Three chart rows flipped in matched pairs to the packet and the mirror; the page's own mid text opens 'Irelia owns this lane' under rows credited to Skill. Added the Bladesurge heal and the Grievous Wounds timing that follows from it.
